cfg_comparison.candidate_vs_retail: not address-comparable. Candidate block/edge counts above differ from retail; the compared structural properties are listed under compared_properties.

compared_properties: cdecl two-argument boundary; context at [esp+4], path at [esp+8]
single ret at 0x004C666C; only tail call is DynObj_UpdateDynTree_11(context) at 0x004C665A
DynObj_UpdateDynTree_11 (0x004CE3D0) writes 0 at context+0xDC8 and returns arg1
live retail: EAX 0x038910B4 equals the context argument
retail file order: .bit, .hmp, .cmd, .ctr, .qsc; allocations at context+0xDC0/0xDC4
divergences: Candidate Terrain_Load is a 12-block wrapper (383 bytes) that calls Terrain_LoadLevel; retail is a 25-block, 1069-byte function.
Retail .bit/.hmp pointer tables, context offsets, QVM registration (CreateTerrainMaterial/CreateTerrainTileMap), Qvm_Load/Execute/Cleanup and Mem_Alloc calls are host-adapted.
Retail clears context+0xDC8 through the tail call; the candidate returns the context but does not perform that write because the port object does not mirror the offset.
Candidate has host-only null guards returning nullptr; retail dereferences its arguments.
limitations: Binary Ninja and radare2 CFG scores are retail-image structure only. They do not measure candidate equivalence.
angr CFGFast is approximate and splits blocks differently; only the exact entry and unresolved-jump result are used as evidence.
No paired retail/candidate runtime capture exists for this native, so no behavioral equivalence is claimed.
